Working at Meta, I knew getting laid off was a possibility. In recent years, layoffs have been happening rapidly in tech, and traditional ideas around job security and the 9-to-5 have been shifting.
I was nearly four years into my role as a program manager at Meta when we were notified that layoffs would be happening in a few weeks, on May 20. At 7 a.m. that morning, I checked my email. No news yet. At 7.02, nothing happened. I kept on refreshing my inbox, and at around 7.14 a.m., I found out my service was no longer needed.
My view has always been that if a company decides my skills are no longer required, that's fair. Because of my faith, I believe that everything happens for a reason. My immediate response was to give praise to God, say goodbye to my colleagues, and put my laptop away.
I have a wife and two kids I need to provide for. I felt prepared for the layoff because I always tried to live below my means. I also had entrepreneurial ideas in my back pocket. I was ready to figure out my next chapter.

The European Commission took two decisions finding non-compliance by Google with the Digital Markets Act (DMA) for self-preferencing its own services on Google Search, and for putting in place restrictions on businesses to direct consumers to alternative, often cheaper, purchase channels on Google Play (steering).
In this regard, the Commission issued Google a fine of €460 million and a fine of €430 million respectively.
Self-preferencing on Google Search
Under the DMA, gatekeepers must not treat their own services more favourably in ranking than third-party services. They have to apply transparent, fair and non-discriminatory conditions to such ranking.
The Commission found that Google gives preferential treatment to its own services, including shopping, hotels, transport and sports results, over those of third parties in Google Search, thereby breaching its obligations under the DMA.
Google displays its own services more prominently in search results, including at the top of the search results page or by using enhanced visuals and filters, while similar third-party services do not have the same prominence.
Google's anti-steering
Under the DMA, app developers that distribute their apps via Google Play should be able to inform customers – free of charge – of alternative, often cheaper, offers, and to direct them to those offers to make purchases, for example on websites or alternative app stores.
The Commission found that Google failed to comply with that obligation.

JSON, short for JavaScript Object Notation, is the plain-text format countless apps and websites use to pass data around. Its official standard, RFC 8259, allows objects, arrays, strings, numbers, true, false, and null. It doesn't allow comments, and it doesn't allow a trailing comma, the extra comma after the last item in a list.

Is It Too Late to Buy Bloom Energy? My Honest Take. - The Motley Fool. Up over 200% since last October, and over 1,400% over the last five years, Bloom Energy (BE +2.81%) has been on an absolute tear. And it's not hard to see why. Bloom has become one of the most important energy companies to the tech industry, mainly because it has something AI companies desperately need: power, and fast.
Bloom's solid oxide fuel cells -- Bloom boxes, as they're sometimes called -- can generate electricity directly at data centers, which allows developers to sidestep the years-long wait for a connection to the grid. This "time to power" advantage has catapulted Bloom from a relatively obscure clean-energy upstart into one of Wall Street's hottest energy stocks.
With such an enormous run behind it, however, the uncomfortable question emerges: Have Bloom's best market days come and gone, or is there still upside ahead?

A man pushed a woman into a deep gorge near Naikwadi in Maharashtra's Kolhapur after she refused to continue their relationship. Police said the accused initially claimed she was missing before surrendering at Bhudargad police station. The police are investigating the alleged killing and the circumstances surrounding her death.
A 25-year-old man has been arrested for pushing a 23-year-old woman to her death in a deep gorge in Maharashtra's Kolhapur district after she refused to continue their relationship. The accused, identified as Shripad Dinkar Wadu, allegedly took Tarannum Bashir Naik to a spot near Naikwadi on Friday morning and pushed her into the gorge after an argument. He later surrendered at Bhudargad police station after initially claiming that the woman was missing. Police are investigating the case.
Shripad and Tarannum lived opposite each other in Avadhut Colony in Gargoti and had been in a relationship, according to a report by ABP Marathi. Tarannum was pursuing engineering studies at a college in Mahagaon. However, after her marriage was arranged, she reportedly told Shripad that they could no longer continue their relationship. The decision then led to disputes between the two.

Trade buzz involving the Boston Red Sox and Philadelphia Phillies star Bryce Harper is already a-buzzing, and it's only the start of October. MLB insider Bob Nightengale sparked all the Harper chatter, which Red Sox fans ran with in all sorts of different directions.
Appearing as a guest on 97.5 The Fanatic, Nightengale suggested that the Phillies will probably shop either/both of Harper and Trea Turner this offseason following another early postseason exit (Nightengale doubted that Philadelphia would trade Kyle Schwarber). When asked who between Harper and Turner would be the likelier trade piece, Nightengale went with Harper.
âYouâd think probably Harper in the sense that Turner doesnât have that [contract] value,â he said. âYouâd have to eat a lot of that contract to move him. Harperâs contract is very reasonable.â
Harper's AAV over the next five seasons is right around $25.4 million per season.
Red Sox fans are envisioning a trade for Bryce Harper in response to insider's intel
Where would Bryce Harper actually fit with the Red Sox?
The Red Sox already have an All-Star first baseman in Willson Contreras. And even if an aging Harper were to move back to the outfield (that would be weird), Boston has a logjam out there, anyway. Some fans have already suggested trading Roman Anthony (gasp!) to make room for Harper. Keep in mind that Harper will turn 34 years old this October.
